label: No/minimal contact
meaning: Was in the household or identified as a contact but had no direct physical interaction with the case or their environment. Captures: not direct contact (Baron); no physical contact (Gayedyu-Dennis); did not have direct physical contact (Dowell; Francesconi); household contact with no direct physical contact (Reichler).
assumptions: None — this is the reference category against which all other classes are estimated.

label: Indirect contact only
key_criterion: Shared environment or fomite exposure with no direct physical contact
meaning: Shared living environment (slept or ate in same room) or had contact with the case's clothing or belongings but no direct physical contact with the person. Captures: slept or ate in the same room / contact with clothing (Gayedyu-Dennis); indirect wet contact and indirect dry contact (Bower).
assumptions: Environmental exposure via fomites or shared space is assumed to carry higher risk than purely epidemiological linkage with no contact. The distinction from the reference is subtle and may not be well-supported across studies — candidate for collapsing into the reference category if the coefficient is not distinguishable.

label: Direct physical contact — no fluids and no nursing
key_criterion: Touched or was in close physical contact with the case but no nursing care and no body fluid exposure
meaning: Touched or was in close physical contact with the case but did not provide nursing care and had no exposure to body fluids. Captures: direct contact but no nursing care (Baron); direct physical contact with index and no nursing care (Reichler); had direct physical contact (Dowell); direct physical contact (Francesconi); direct dry contact (Bower); touched the patient (International Commission Sudan); slept or ate in same room / contact with clothing / direct physical contact (Gayedyu-Dennis).
assumptions: Direct physical contact without nursing is assumed not to involve body fluid exposure. This is not always true (e.g. an embrace could involve sweat or vomit) but is the best available approximation given how studies report it.

label: Nursing care — no body fluids
key_criterion: Actively cared for the case with no documented body fluid exposure
meaning: Actively cared for the case — bathing; feeding; administering medication — implying sustained close contact but no documented body fluid exposure. Captures: direct contact and nursing care (Baron); nursed the patient (International Commission Sudan); provided care (Jezek); nursing care with no or some protection but no contact with body fluids (Reichler); provided nursing care (Francesconi).
assumptions: Nursing care implies direct physical contact — a row reporting nursing without explicit mention of direct contact is assumed to involve direct contact. This is biologically necessary and consistent with how Bower defines direct wet contact. If a study reports both nursing and body fluid contact for the same group that group maps to Class 4 rather than Class 3.

label: Body fluid contact
key_criterion: Documented exposure to blood or body fluids from the case
meaning: Documented exposure to blood; vomit; diarrhoea; sweat or other body fluids from the case whether during nursing or otherwise. Captures: contact with body fluids of index (Gayedyu-Dennis); contact with body fluids (Francesconi); nursing care and contact with body fluids (Reichler); direct wet contact and handled fluids (Bower); high-risk percutaneous or mucous membrane exposure to blood or body fluids (Reaves); high-risk contact with body fluids linen or clothes (Henao-Restrepo).
assumptions: Body fluid contact is treated as a single class regardless of route (mucous membrane; skin; percutaneous) because most studies do not disaggregate by route. Where a study reports both nursing and body fluid contact for the same group that group maps here rather than to Class 3.

label: Handled corpse
key_criterion: Participated in funeral preparation washing or burial of a confirmed case
meaning: Participated in funeral preparation; washing; or burial of a confirmed case. Captures: handled corpse (Bower); high-risk exposure including corpse handling (Reaves).
assumptions: Treated as a separate class from body fluid contact because post-mortem viral load is substantially higher than during illness and funeral practices are a well-documented distinct transmission route in Ebola. Not assumed a priori to be strictly higher risk than Class 4 — the ordering reflects prior literature but the model estimates this freely. This class is reported by few studies and should be treated as exploratory if the coefficient is poorly identified.
